verdict.rationale: vLLM's docs list integer quantization including INT8, INT4, GPTQ/AWQ and GGUF, and say quantization trades precision for a smaller memory footprint. That covers the 4-bit to 8-bit range directly. The sub-4-bit 'very low-bit' end is never explicitly documented, so coverage of the full range is partial. The older community remark that 4-bit was unsupported predates the current docs listing INT4/GPTQ/AWQ, so it does not dispute the claim. missing for 10: explicit documentation of sub-4-bit (2-3 bit) integer quantization, independent hands-on corroboration of memory savings across the bit range.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can reduce memory footprint using integer quantization ranging from very low-bit to 8-bit precision

citations.quote: Quantization: FP8, MXFP8/MXFP4, NVFP4, INT8, INT4, GPTQ/AWQ, GGUF, compressed-tensors, ModelOpt, TorchAO, and more
